nodes.title: Pilot (E1, average concurrency in single digits): live always-on STT stays MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming (southindia) with gpt-live-transcribe D4 as automatic fallback, streaming the whole session; Nemotron-3.5-ASR-streaming-0.6B (auto-LID, never hi-IN) runs as an OFFLINE shadow on consented E1 recordings plus one Chennai latency probe against an Azure Central India T4, with no production dependency. Rationale: below ~1.2-1.6 average concurrent sessions a warm GPU pair (~$845-1,175/month) costs more than the API; MAI ties or beats D4 (dCER -0.007, 80% CI [-0.017, 0.003]; answers 78/78) and is fastest from India (68 ms after commit). Reverse if: MAI bills above D4 or loses to D4 on E1 (then D4), or average concurrency during the pilot exceeds ~2 sessions (then self-host earlier).

At scale (average concurrency >= ~20 and E1 passed): the always-on ear (partials, barge-in confirmation, endpoint text) is self-hosted Nemotron-3.5-ASR-streaming-0.6B @ ea30d66 at 320 ms chunks, auto-LID plus script guard, in India (Azure Central India first; AWS ap-south-1 if quota clears and it is cheaper), planned at 64 streams per L4 (half the measured 128), fleet ceil(C/cap)x1.2+1, autoscaled, on-demand only, with the API lane as a mid-session hot fallback. Graded-answer turns get a second pass (MAI-Transcribe-2, or self-hosted Qwen3-ASR-1.7B) until E1 or a child fine-tune shows Nemotron within a pre-registered margin on numbers and graded answers. Cost $0.04-0.11 per session-hour incl. idle headroom and 0.5% fallback vs $1.02 D4. Reverse if: E1 shows Nemotron (with guard) worse than D4/MAI beyond the margin on ungraded-turn intent too, or it emits text in child silence/background speech that MAI does not, or a production serving stack cannot hold p95 added lag <= 300 ms at 64 streams, or MAI is metered below ~$0.10/h (then the API is within ops-cost noise).

Any auto-LID STT output (Nemotron first) passes a deterministic script guard: tokens outside Devanagari, Latin, digits and punctuation are dropped and the utterance is flagged low-confidence (re-ask or second pass, never graded). Reason: Nemotron auto-LID wrote 3-5/180 synthetic clips in Vietnamese/Arabic script, and forcing hi-IN instead empties English (0/12). Reverse if: on E1 the guard drops real child speech in more than 1% of turns, or LID errors stop appearing after a child fine-tune.

Emotion/prosody 'hearing' is a separate sidecar on the same always-on audio, not an STT feature: continuous features (F0 level/range, energy, speaking rate from token timing, pause and response latency, voice quality, laughter/sigh events) relative to the child's own session baseline, mapped to Director signals, never to emotion labels or stored categories; no categorical SER (best published macro-F1 ~0.43 on adults, nothing for child Hinglish). Features may only shape pacing until a pre-registered E1 test shows a feature-using policy beats transcript-only. Reverse if: that E1 test fails (drop the lane), or a measured child-speech affect model passes it (allow a learned layer).

STT v3 accuracy vs D4/MAI with 80% intervals (synthetic TTS child-Hinglish corpus, n=180 speech; non-speech n=12 for API arms, n=30 for open arms; same score.mjs/score2.mjs; item-level paired bootstrap dCER over 30 items; Wilson 80% for counts; evals/stt-v3/results/tables-stt-v3.md). D4 cer 0.028, numbers 92/96 [0.924,0.978], answers 76/78 [0.940,0.989]; MAI-Tx-2 batch 0.017, dCER -0.011 [-0.022,0.001], 91/96, 78/78 [0.979,1]; MAI-Tx-2-Streaming 0.021, dCER -0.007 [-0.017,0.003], 90/96, 78/78; Qwen3-ASR-1.7B auto 0.031, dCER +0.003 [-0.005,0.012], 84/96 [0.825,0.912], 70/78 [0.845,0.934]; Nemotron auto 320 ms 0.046, dCER +0.018 [0.008,0.029], 84/96 [0.825,0.912], 74/78 [0.906,0.972], non-speech 0/30 [0,0.052]. Nemotron's numbers interval does not overlap D4's; answers overlap. Real-child accuracy unmeasured (E1).

STT always-on cost model (arithmetic, not a billing measurement; prices from Azure Retail API and AWS Pricing API 2026-10-04; capacity from the stt-v3 L4 load test, T4 capacity estimated). Assumptions: session-h/month = 180 x peak concurrency C (6 peak-equivalent h/day); Nemotron 64 streams/L4 (measured limit 128 halved), 32/T4 [estimate]; fleet ceil(C/cap)x1.2+1; autoscaled = full fleet 8 h, max(2, 25%) warm 16 h; 0.5% of session-hours fail over to D4. $/session-hour at C=100/1,000/10,000: Nemotron Azure CI T4 autoscaled 0.082/0.051/0.049 (flat 24 h 0.144/0.098/0.092); AWS ap-south-1 L4 autoscaled 0.108/0.048/0.042; gpt-live-transcribe 1.02; Azure Speech RT+LID 1.30 PAYG, 0.845/0.52/0.52 best commitment tier; MAI-Tx-2 placeholder 0.36 (no meter). C=10,000 needs ~190 L4 or ~377 T4 in India; ap-south-1 G/VT quota 0.

Tried (bench): Nemotron-3.5 streaming auto-LID as the turn-final transcript the Director grades, replacing D4/MAI. Broke: numbers 84/96 [80% 0.825,0.912] vs D4 92/96 [0.924,0.978] (non-overlapping), English answers 9-11/12, dCER +0.018 [0.008,0.029], noisy cer about 2x D4 at 10 dB SNR. Keep it as the always-on ear; grade from a second pass until E1 or a child fine-tune closes the gap.

Tried (desk): running Sarvam Saaras in our own cloud to satisfy the self-host-only rule. Broke: Saaras v4 is API-only (no weights); Saaras v3 exists only as an encrypted AWS SageMaker Marketplace package at a $5,000/month contract plus instance cost, the weights are not ours and cannot be fine-tuned on child audio, and its published Hindi WER (~22 on IndicVoices) gives no reason to pay. The API (~$0.35/h) stays reference-only.

Tried (costed): paying a per-session-hour STT API for the always-on ear at scale. Broke: gpt-live-transcribe $1.02/session-h = $184k/month at 1,000 peak concurrent children and $1.84M at 10,000 (Azure Speech RT+LID at best commitment tier $0.52), vs $0.04-0.05 self-hosted Nemotron incl. idle headroom ($8-9k/month at 1,000). Fine for the pilot below ~1.2-1.6 average concurrent sessions; not past ~20.

Tried (design): spot GPUs for the live STT lane (spot L4 ~30-45% cheaper). Broke: a reclaim ends every child's stream on that GPU at once (up to 64-128 children) with a 161 s cold start to replace it; only usable for the offline shadow and the bench, or as a surplus replica if client failover to the API lane is proven.
